text:
Alex Chen: heads up — q-ranker-v2-int8 on the new bringup bench shows an unexpected NDCG drop vs fp16. Posted raw numbers below, wondering if this is quant or something else. :thinking: Mira Patel: can you paste the exact eval command and the output? Alex Chen: sure — running locally with the harness:```./run_eval.sh --model q-ranker-v2-int8 --candidates data/cands_pruned.jsonl --queries eval/queries_core.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --preproc-version 3 --stable-order false```Results (fp16 baseline / q-int8): - ndcg@10: 0.412 -> 0.396 (-3.9%) - mrr: 0.278 -> 0.265 (-4.7%) - sample latency: 38ms -> 29ms James O'Neill: ~4% NDCG is non-trivial. Two immediate suspects: tokenizer/preproc drift, or candidate ordering (stable sort). Also check eval harness used the same scoring threshold and tie-breaking. Alex Chen: note: the inference container for int8 used fast-tokenizer-v3 and our eval harness image still had fast-tokenizer-v2. I also flipped candidate ordering to length-first for pruning earlier this week. Sara Gomez: re-run with identical preprocess chain (preproc-version=2) and ensure stable ordering (stable-order=true). Candidate ordering differences can reorder the topK which kills NDCG. Alex Chen: re-ran with preproc-v2 + stable-order=true — command:```./run_eval.sh --model q-ranker-v2-int8 --preproc-version 2 --stable-order true```Output: ndcg@10: 0.412 -> 0.411 (-0.2%), mrr: 0.278 -> 0.277 (-0.4%). Much better. Looks like preprocessing/tokenization + ordering explained the bulk of the gap. eval-bot: eval job complete (job id: ej-9012) — q-int8-with-preproc-v2: ndcg@10=0.411, mrr=0.277. Alex Chen: short diagnostics I ran: diff tokens between fp16 and int8 run for a few failing queries showed subtle whitespace stripping and HTML tag removal in v3 tokenizer. Example: fp16 tokens started with [CLS] "

", v3 stripped "

". Also candidate list ordering changed after length-prune because ties weren't stable. James O'Neill: good catch. Action items: 1) add tokenization parity smoke in bringup pipeline, 2) enforce stable candidate ordering in pruning script, 3) add an eval harness flag that fails if preprocessing metadata mismatch. Sara Gomez: I'll take (2) and (3), will follow up with small PR for pruning tool to add --stable-sort and metadata emit. Alex Chen: I'll open PR for the bringup smoke tests (tokenization parity + spot-check NDCG delta threshold). Created draft PR #4823. CCing @Mira and @Sara for review. Mira Patel: :thumbsup: can we also add a tiny unit test to compare token sequences for 50 random queries between any new model container and the harness image before full eval runs? If mismatch > 0.5% queries fail, block. Alex Chen: yes — plan to add that in the PR. Also adding note to the runbook: "When bringing up quantized models, always run tokenization-parity and stable-order checks before large-scale evals." deploy-bot: deploy check: container q-ranker-v2-int8 image build succeeded (img:registry/redwood/q-ranker-v2:int8-20260321) — no infra issues. Alex Chen: thanks all — closing this thread once PRs land. Will follow up with final numbers in the bringup ticket. :rocket:
